seo.shortDescription: Searchable U.S. duty table for all 559 HTS Chapter 72 iron and steel lines: steel is Free at base but pays the 50% Section 232 tariff on its full value from every country (UK 25%), China 75%. Pig iron, ferroalloys and scrap are outside Section 232.

overview.intro:
Chapter 72 covers iron and steel: pig iron, ferroalloys, direct-reduced iron and scrap (7201–7205), and the steel mill products made from them, from slabs and billets to hot-rolled, cold-rolled and galvanized sheet, plate, bars, rebar, wire rod, shapes and wire in carbon, stainless and alloy steel (7206–7229). **534 of the 559 tariff lines are Free** under the general rate; only the ferroalloys pay a base duty (1.1% to 10%).

What decides the cost is **Section 232**. Every steel mill product (505 lines in 7206–7229) pays **an extra 50% of its full customs value** from every country (heading 9903.82.02): Canada, Mexico, the EU, Japan and Korea included. The only lower rate is **25% for UK steel** at least 95% melted and poured in the United Kingdom (9903.82.04). FTA and USMCA claims do not reduce it. Chinese steel pays another **25% under Section 301**, so 75% in total. Pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders are **outside Section 232**; some of them pay the 2026 Section 301 duties instead.

On top of the tariff, many steel products carry **antidumping and countervailing duties** set company by company by the Commerce Department (hot-rolled, cold-rolled and corrosion-resistant flat steel, plate, rebar, wire rod, stainless sheet). They are not part of this table or the tariff calculator; see Tariff updates and Import documents.

productGroups.label: Pig iron & spiegeleisen
productGroups.blurb: Nonalloy and alloy pig iron and spiegeleisen in pigs, blocks or other primary forms: 4 lines, all Free. Not covered by Section 232; one line (spiegeleisen) pays the 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Ferroalloys
productGroups.blurb: Ferromanganese, ferrosilicon, silicomanganese, ferrochromium, ferronickel, ferromolybdenum, ferrotungsten, ferrotitanium, ferrovanadium, ferroniobium: the only dutiable lines in the chapter (1.1% to 10%). Not covered by Section 232; ferrosilicon and ferrovanadium carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Direct-reduced iron (DRI, HBI)
productGroups.blurb: Ferrous products from direct reduction of iron ore (DRI, hot-briquetted iron) and other spongy ferrous products: 2 lines, Free. Not covered by Section 232; DRI from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

productGroups.label: Ferrous waste & scrap
productGroups.blurb: Cast-iron, stainless, alloy and carbon steel scrap, turnings and remelting scrap ingots: 14 lines, all Free. Not covered by Section 232 and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so only China pays extra.

productGroups.label: Iron & steel granules and powders
productGroups.blurb: Granules and powders of pig iron, iron or steel: 3 lines, Free. Not covered by Section 232; pay the 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Iron & nonalloy steel ingots
productGroups.blurb: Iron and nonalloy steel in ingots or other primary forms: 2 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Semifinished steel (slabs, billets)
productGroups.blurb: Semifinished nonalloy steel: slabs, billets, blooms and other semis: 9 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Hot-rolled flat steel (600 mm+)
productGroups.blurb: Hot-rolled nonalloy flat products 600 mm or wider, in coils (HRC) or cut lengths, including plate: 32 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Several AD/CVD orders (hot-rolled, cut-to-length plate).

productGroups.label: Cold-rolled flat steel (600 mm+)
productGroups.blurb: Cold-rolled (cold-reduced) nonalloy flat products 600 mm or wider, not clad or coated: 22 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Cold-rolled AD/CVD orders apply.

productGroups.label: Coated flat steel (600 mm+)
productGroups.blurb: Galvanized, galvalume, tinplate, tin-free, electrolytic and painted nonalloy flat products 600 mm or wider: 21 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Corrosion-resistant (CORE) orders and the 2026 tin mill investigations.

productGroups.label: Narrow flat steel (under 600 mm)
productGroups.blurb: Hot- and cold-rolled nonalloy flat products under 600 mm wide, not clad or coated (strip, universal mill plate): 25 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Narrow coated flat steel
productGroups.blurb: Clad, plated or coated nonalloy flat products under 600 mm wide (tinned, galvanized, painted strip): 10 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Wire rod (hot-rolled, in coils)
productGroups.blurb: Hot-rolled nonalloy bars and rods in irregularly wound coils: wire rod and rebar in coils: 12 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Wire rod AD/CVD orders apply.

productGroups.label: Hot-rolled bars & rebar
productGroups.blurb: Other nonalloy bars and rods, hot-rolled or forged, including straight concrete reinforcing bar (rebar): 18 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Rebar AD/CVD orders on seven countries.

productGroups.label: Cold-finished bars
productGroups.blurb: Other nonalloy bars and rods, cold-formed or cold-finished (bright bar): 12 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Angles, shapes & sections
productGroups.blurb: Nonalloy angles, shapes and sections: I-beams, H-beams, channels, angles, sheet piling profiles: 18 lines, Free. Hot-rolled shapes pay +50% Section 232; cold-formed shapes (7216.61, 7216.69, 7216.91.00.90) are outside it.

productGroups.label: Nonalloy steel wire
productGroups.blurb: Wire of iron or nonalloy steel, uncoated, galvanized or copper-plated: 48 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Stainless semifinished
productGroups.blurb: Stainless steel in ingots and semifinished products (slabs, billets): 9 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Stainless flat (600 mm+)
productGroups.blurb: Flat-rolled stainless steel 600 mm or wider: hot-rolled plate, cold-rolled sheet (304, 316, 430): 76 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Stainless sheet and strip AD/CVD orders apply.

productGroups.label: Stainless strip (under 600 mm)
productGroups.blurb: Flat-rolled stainless steel under 600 mm wide, including razor blade steel: 24 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Stainless wire rod
productGroups.blurb: Hot-rolled stainless bars and rods in irregularly wound coils: 6 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Stainless bars & shapes
productGroups.blurb: Other stainless bars, rods, angles, shapes and sections: 31 lines, Free; +50% Section 232. Stainless bar from India is under an AD order.

productGroups.label: Stainless wire
productGroups.blurb: Wire of stainless steel, including spring round wire: 8 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy steel semifinished
productGroups.blurb: Other alloy steel in ingots and semifinished forms: 11 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy flat steel (600 mm+)
productGroups.blurb: Flat-rolled other alloy steel 600 mm or wider, including grain-oriented and non-oriented electrical steel: 28 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy flat steel (under 600 mm)
productGroups.blurb: Flat-rolled other alloy steel under 600 mm wide, including electrical steel strip and high-speed steel: 26 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy wire rod
productGroups.blurb: Other alloy steel bars and rods, hot-rolled, in irregularly wound coils: 14 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy bars, shapes & drill rods
productGroups.blurb: Other alloy steel bars and rods, angles, shapes and sections, and hollow drill bars: 35 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Alloy steel wire
productGroups.blurb: Wire of other alloy steel, including silico-manganese and high-speed steel wire: 11 lines, Free; +50% Section 232.

workedExamples.title: $700,000 of hot-rolled coil from South Korea
workedExamples.body: Hot-rolled coil is **Free** under the general rate, but it is a Section 232 steel article, so it pays **+50% of its full value** (9903.82.02): **$350,000**. The KORUS FTA does not help, because note 16(b) collects the Section 232 duty on top of any FTA rate, and the 2026 Section 301 duty on Korea does not apply to Section 232 steel (note 52(f)(1)). Check also whether the producer is under the hot-rolled antidumping order on Korea.

workedExamples.title: Galvanized sheet from Mexico, with a USMCA certification
workedExamples.body: Galvanized flat steel is **Free**, and USMCA makes it Free again, but Section 232 still charges **+50%** (9903.82.02): Mexican steel has had no Section 232 exemption since March 12, 2025. A lower 25% rate (9903.82.18) exists only for limited quantities that Commerce authorizes for Canadian or Mexican producers that commit to new U.S. steelmaking capacity. Since December 19, 2025, corrosion-resistant steel from Mexico is also under antidumping and countervailing duty orders.

workedExamples.title: Cold-rolled stainless sheet from China
workedExamples.body: Free at base, plus **50%** Section 232 (9903.82.02) and **25%** Section 301 (note 31, 9903.91.01): **75%**, or $75,000 on $100,000. The 2026 Section 301 duty on China (12.5%) does not apply to Section 232 steel. Stainless sheet and strip from China is also under antidumping and countervailing duty orders.

workedExamples.title: UK steel melted and poured in the United Kingdom
workedExamples.body: Grain-oriented electrical steel of the UK pays **+25%** (9903.82.04) instead of 50% when at least 95% of its steel was melted and poured in the UK (note 16(d)); Tata Steel UK steel melted in the Netherlands also counts until January 1, 2028. Without that proof it pays the full **50%**.

workedExamples.title: Ferrosilicon from Brazil
workedExamples.body: Ferroalloys are outside Section 232. This line pays its **1.5%** base rate, **+25%** under the Section 301 action on Brazil (9903.05.01) and **+12.5%** under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.27): **39%**. Ferrosilicon from Brazil, Kazakhstan and Malaysia is also under antidumping and countervailing duty orders (May 2025).

workedExamples.title: Heavy melting scrap from Canada
workedExamples.body: Ferrous scrap is **Free**, is not a Section 232 steel article, and is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (9903.05.86), so Canadian scrap pays **no duty**, with or without a USMCA claim. Only Chinese scrap pays extra (25%, Section 301 List 3).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1 (definitions).** (a) *Pig iron*: iron-carbon alloys not usefully malleable, with more than 2% carbon (and limits on chromium, manganese, phosphorus, silicon and other elements). (b) *Spiegeleisen*: as pig iron, with more than 6% but not more than 30% manganese. (c) *Ferroalloys*: alloys in primary, continuously cast, granular or powder forms, used as additives, deoxidants or desulfurizing agents in ferrous metallurgy, generally not usefully malleable, with at least 4% iron and more than 10% chromium, 30% manganese, 3% phosphorus, 8% silicon or 10% other elements (copper at most 10%). (d) *Steel*: ferrous materials other than those of heading 7203 that are usefully malleable and contain 2% or less carbon (chromium steels may contain more). (e) *Stainless steel*: alloy steel with 1.2% or less carbon and 10.5% or more chromium. (f) *Other alloy steel*: steel that is not stainless and contains at least one element above a threshold (for example 0.3% chromium, 1.65% manganese, 0.08% molybdenum, 0.3% nickel, 0.6% silicon, 0.0008% boron). (g) *Remelting scrap ingots*; (h) *Granules*; (ij) *Semifinished products*: continuous cast or primary hot-rolled or roughly forged products of solid section, not in coils. (k) *Flat-rolled products*: rolled products of solid rectangular section in coils, or straight lengths at least 10 times as wide as thick (under 4.75 mm) or wider than 150 mm and at least twice the thickness (4.75 mm or more). (l) *Bars and rods, hot-rolled, in irregularly wound coils*; (m) *Other bars and rods*; (n) *Angles, shapes and sections* (not products of heading 7301 or 7302); (o) *Wire*: cold-formed products in coils; (p) *Hollow drill bars and rods*.

**Note 2.** Ferrous metals clad with another ferrous metal are classified as the ferrous metal predominating by weight.

**Note 3.** Iron or steel products obtained by electrolytic deposition, pressure casting or sintering are classified by form, composition and appearance with the similar hot-rolled products.

**Subheading notes.** Define alloy pig iron, nonalloy free-cutting steel, silicon electrical steel (0.6% to 6% silicon, at most 0.08% carbon), high-speed steel and silico-manganese steel, and classify ferroalloys as binary, ternary or quaternary by how many elements exceed the note 1(c) minimums.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**1.** Defines *high-strength steel* (flat-rolled, minimum yield point 275 MPa under 3 mm or 355 MPa at 3 mm or more), *universal mill plate*, *concrete reinforcing bars and rods*, *razor blade steel*, *tool steel*, *chipper knife steel*, *heat-resisting steel* and *ball-bearing steel*.

**2.** "Further worked" means surface treatments such as polishing, artificial oxidation, phosphatizing, metal or nonmetallic coating, or cladding.

**3.** No allowance or reduction of duties is made for partial damage or loss from discoloration or rust occurring before entry.

Statistical notes define high-nickel alloy steel, the ISRI scrap grades used in 7204, advanced and ultra high-strength steel, tire cord-quality, cold-heading-quality and welding-quality wire rod, and spring round wire.

seo.title: Steel Tariff Updates 2025–2026: 50% Section 232, Full-Value Rule, Canada, Mexico, UK (HTS Ch. 72) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every U.S. steel tariff change since 2025 with Federal Register citations: Section 232 restored to 25% for all countries (March 2025), raised to 50% (June 2025), rebuilt on full value (April 2026), the UK's 25% rate, the end of the IEEPA duties, and the new steel AD/CVD orders.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 72 today. Base rates barely moved: steel is Free in both, and the only change is that ferrosilicon manganese (7202.30.00.00) was split into two statistical lines at the same 3.9%.

The extra duties changed a lot. In January 2025, steel paid 25% under Section 232, but Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Korea, the EU, Japan, the UK and Ukraine were exempt or under quotas. Proclamation 10896 ended all of those arrangements and the product exclusions on **March 12, 2025**; Proclamation 10947 raised the rate to **50% on June 4, 2025** (UK stayed at 25%); and Proclamation 11021 rebuilt the program on **April 6, 2026** as heading 9903.82.02, charged on the **full customs value**. The IEEPA duties never added to Section 232 steel for most countries and **ended on February 24, 2026**; the Section 122 surcharge and the 2026 Section 301 duties also leave Section 232 steel alone. China's Section 301 duty (25%) does stack.

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders cover much of the chapter. They are company-specific, listed below for reference, and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 72 from any country: Section 232 steel (note 16), China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The main antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 72 products are listed for reference; the calculator does not model them. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 steel, on the full customs value
inEffect.before: +25% (9903.80.01), with Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Australia, Brazil and Korea exempt or under quotas, and the EU, Japan and UK under tariff-rate quotas
inEffect.exemption: Covers 505 lines: all of 7206–7215, 7217–7229 and the hot-rolled shapes of 7216 (note 16(c)(iii); 7216.91.00.10 as a derivative under (iv)). Pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders (7201–7205) and cold-formed shapes (7216.61, 7216.69, 7216.91.00.90) are not covered. There are no country exemptions, quotas or product exclusions: Proclamation 10896 ended them on March 12, 2025. Note 16(b): the duty is collected on top of any FTA or USMCA special rate. Lower rates only for UK steel at least 95% UK-melted (9903.82.04, 25%) and for limited Canadian or Mexican quantities that Commerce authorizes (9903.82.18, 25%). Russia uses 9903.82.14 (also 50%). Goods under 9903.82.02 do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)).

inEffect.exemption: Note 16(d): applies only when at least 95% of the steel was melted and poured in the United Kingdom; Commerce (91 FR 23056) lets Tata Steel UK steel melted and poured in the Netherlands count as UK until January 1, 2028. Executive Order 14309 contemplates a quota at the normal tariff rate for UK steel, but none has been established. UK steel that does not meet the 95% test pays 50% under 9903.82.02.

inEffect.measure: Section 301: note 31 (2024 review), Lists 3 and 4A, and the 2026 action
inEffect.now: +25% on steel (on top of 50% Section 232 = 75%); 25% to 37.5% extra on pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders
inEffect.exemption: Note 31 (9903.91.01) adds 25% to 486 lines, almost all steel mill products, since September 27, 2024; List 3 (9903.88.03) covers most of 7201–7205 and some 7216 lines; List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%) covers 20 wire, strip and bar lines. These stack with Section 232. Forged bars (7214.10), ferromolybdenum (7202.70) and two other ferroalloy lines are on none of these lists. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China (9903.05.31) applies only to the 19 non-Section 232 lines outside the note 52(b) exemption list. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue during the four-year review.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese steel sheet, plate, bar or wire pays 75% of its value; Chinese ferrosilicon pays its base rate plus 37.5%.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, UK, Russia and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate) on 19 lines
inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 steel (note 52(f)(1), 9903.05.90). Of the 54 other lines, pig iron, most ferroalloys, DRI and all scrap are on the general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86). It charges spiegeleisen (7201.50.60), ferrosilicon (7202.21, 7202.29), ferromolybdenum (7202.70), ferrovanadium (7202.92), other ferroalloys (7202.99), iron and steel powders (7205) and cold-formed shapes (7216.61, 7216.69, 7216.91.00.90). USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

It does charge 25 other lines: ferrosilicon, ferromolybdenum, ferrovanadium and other ferroalloys (7202.21, 7202.29, 7202.70, 7202.92, 7202.99), cast-iron and carbon steel scrap (7204.10, 7204.29, 7204.49, 7204.50), powders (7205) and cold-formed shapes. Ferrosilicon from Brazil also carries AD/CVD.

changes.title: No Chapter 72 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 557 of 559 Chapter 72 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. Ferrosilicon manganese 7202.30.00.00 was split into 7202.30.00.60 (not more than 0.10% carbon) and 7202.30.00.90 (other), both at the unchanged 3.9%.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29). Note 29 has no Section 232 carve-out, so it will add to the 50% on Nicaraguan steel. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Tin mill products from China: preliminary dumping and subsidy findings
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found dumping (September 21, 2026) and countervailable subsidies (September 15, 2026) on tin mill products from China, with critical circumstances, and is investigating tin mill products from Taiwan and Türkiye (initiated May 5, 2026). Cash deposits apply from the preliminary determinations; orders depend on the final Commerce and ITC decisions. Tin mill products (tinplate and tin-free steel) enter mainly under 7210.11, 7210.12, 7210.50, 7212.10 and 7212.50, and 7225.99 or 7226.99 if of alloy steel.

changes.title: New AD/CVD orders on rebar (Bulgaria, Egypt, Vietnam) and wire rod (Algeria)
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping duty orders on steel concrete reinforcing bar from Bulgaria, Egypt and Vietnam, countervailing duty orders on rebar from Egypt and Vietnam, and a countervailing duty order on carbon and alloy steel wire rod from Algeria. Rebar is classified mainly in 7213.10, 7214.20 and 7228.30; wire rod in 7213 and 7227.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian direct-reduced iron
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on products of Canada in the note 51(b)(3) list, which includes direct-reduced iron (7203.10.00); it is charged even on USMCA goods. The start moved from August 19 to August 22, 2026 (Proclamation 11056), and from September 15, 2026 it applies in addition to any Section 232 duty (Proclamation 11065). No other Chapter 72 line is on the list.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: steel mill products exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. They do not apply to Section 232 steel (note 52(f)(1)), and pig iron, most ferroalloys, DRI and scrap are on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). In Chapter 72 they charge 19 lines: spiegeleisen, ferrosilicon, ferromolybdenum, ferrovanadium, other ferroalloys, iron and steel powders and cold-formed shapes. USMCA goods are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It never applied to Section 232 steel (Proclamation 11012 clause 4; note 2(aa)(v)(2)), and most ferroalloys and stainless scrap (7204.21) were on its product exemption list (9903.03.03).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil: steel exempt, ferroalloys and scrap not
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Section 232 steel is excluded (note 50(a)(vi)(1)), so it reaches only some Brazilian ferroalloys (notably ferrosilicon), most scrap, powders and cold-formed shapes: 25 Chapter 72 lines.

changes.title: AD and CVD orders on rebar from Algeria
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping duty order (April 29, 2026) and a countervailing duty order (July 6, 2026) on steel concrete reinforcing bar from Algeria.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032 adjusts the metals program
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, steel content counts as U.S.-melted when at least 85% (by weight) was melted and poured in the United States, and new rates apply to industrial and mobile equipment derivatives. Nothing changed for Chapter 72 steel articles: they stay at 50% (UK 25%).

changes.title: Non-oriented electrical steel orders continued
changes.detail: After second five-year reviews, Commerce continued the 2014 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on non-oriented electrical steel (7225.19, 7226.19) from China, Germany, Japan, Korea, Sweden and Taiwan, applicable May 13, 2026.
changes.countries: China, Germany, Japan, Korea, Sweden, Taiwan

changes.title: Commerce corrects the Section 232 annex; Tata Steel UK clarified
changes.detail: Commerce added heading 9903.82.01 (articles on the lists with no steel, aluminum or copper pay no Section 232 duty) from April 6, 2026, and clarified that UK steel made by Tata Steel UK from steel melted and poured in the Netherlands may enter at the UK rate (9903.82.04) and count toward the 95% test until January 1, 2028.

changes.title: Commerce opens the 25% route for Canadian and Mexican steel producers
changes.detail: Commerce set out how steel and aluminum producers with plants in Canada or Mexico that supply U.S. vehicle makers can apply for a tariff reduction of up to half (not below 25%), limited to quantities equal to newly committed U.S. primary steel or aluminum capacity. Approved steel enters under 9903.82.18 (+25%) if it qualifies for USMCA and was melted and poured in Canada or Mexico.

changes.title: Rebar orders on Mexico and Türkiye continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping duty order on rebar from Mexico and the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on rebar from Türkiye after five-year reviews.

changes.title: Section 232 metals program rebuilt on full value (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier steel headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value regardless of metal content. Steel articles of Chapter 72 stay at 50% (9903.82.02); UK products need at least 95% UK-melted steel for the 25% rate (9903.82.04); Russian steel uses 9903.82.14. Manufacturing drawback is allowed only for certain derivative articles of trade-agreement partners, not for Chapter 72 steel articles; goods entering a foreign-trade zone must take privileged foreign status. The derivatives inclusions process ended.

changes.title: Wire rod orders continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping duty orders on carbon and certain alloy steel wire rod from Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Moldova and Trinidad and Tobago and the countervailing duty order on Brazil (March 2, 2026), and the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on China (January 27, 2026).
changes.countries: Brazil, China, Indonesia, Mexico, Moldova, Trinidad and Tobago

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 steel outside it
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Proclamation 11012 says it does not apply in addition to Section 232 duties, so steel mill products paid only the 50%. Most ferroalloys and stainless scrap (7204.21) were on its exemption list (9903.03.03), and USMCA goods were exempt; pig iron, DRI, other scrap, ferrosilicon, ferromolybdenum, ferrovanadium, powders and cold-formed shapes paid the 10%.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026. Section 232 steel duties are not IEEPA duties and continued unchanged. For Chapter 72, the IEEPA duties had mattered mainly for pig iron, ferroalloys, scrap and other non-Section 232 lines.

changes.title: New AD/CVD orders on corrosion-resistant steel from 10 countries
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping duty orders on corrosion-resistant (galvanized and other coated) steel from Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, the Netherlands, South Africa, Taiwan, Türkiye, the United Arab Emirates and Vietnam, and countervailing duty orders on Brazil, Canada, Mexico and Vietnam. They add to the 2016 orders on China, India, Italy, Korea and Taiwan, continued in 2022. In March and April 2026 Commerce opened circumvention inquiries on the CORE orders on China, Korea and Vietnam.
changes.countries: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, Netherlands, South Africa, Taiwan, Türkiye, UAE, Vietnam

changes.title: Authority to halve Section 232 for some Canadian and Mexican steel
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 (medium- and heavy-duty vehicles) authorized Commerce to cut the Section 232 steel and aluminum duty by up to half, but not below 25%, for limited quantities from Canadian or Mexican producers that supply U.S. vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. capacity. The goods must qualify for USMCA and be melted and poured in Canada or Mexico (heading 9903.82.18).

changes.title: Hot-rolled steel orders on six countries continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain hot-rolled carbon steel flat products from India, Indonesia, China, Taiwan, Thailand and Ukraine.
changes.countries: India, Indonesia, China, Taiwan, Thailand, Ukraine

changes.title: UK Economic Prosperity Deal: UK steel stays at 25%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14309, implementing the U.S.-UK Economic Prosperity Deal, directed Commerce to design a tariff-rate quota for UK steel at a time it deems appropriate; the deal's general terms speak of a quota at most-favored-nation rates once the UK meets U.S. supply-chain and ownership requirements. No quota has been established. UK steel stays at 25% under Proclamation 10947; since April 6, 2026 that rate requires at least 95% UK-melted steel.

changes.title: Section 232 steel tariff doubled to 50%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 steel and aluminum duties from 25% to 50% for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4, 2025, except for the UK (25%). It also amended Executive Order 14289 so that steel subject to Section 232 no longer paid the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties, and ruled out drawback.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on ferrosilicon
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on ferrosilicon (7202.21, 7202.29) from Brazil, Kazakhstan and Malaysia.

changes.title: Non-stacking order: Canada and Mexico IEEPA duty in place of Section 232
changes.detail: Executive Order 14289, retroactive to March 4, 2025, said goods of Canada and Mexico subject to the IEEPA duties would not also pay the Section 232 steel duty. Proclamation 10947 reversed the order of precedence from June 4, 2025: Section 232 steel no longer paid the IEEPA duties.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff excludes Section 232 steel
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025 but excluded steel articles and derivatives subject to Section 232 (Annex II). Non-Section 232 Chapter 72 lines paid it unless exempted. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: All Section 232 steel exemptions, quotas and exclusions end
changes.detail: Proclamation 10896 restored the full 25% Section 232 duty on steel from Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, South Korea, the EU, Japan, the UK and Ukraine by ending their exemptions, quotas and tariff-rate quotas, and stopped new product exclusions. General approved exclusions ended March 12, 2025; granted exclusions ran until they expired or were used up.
changes.countries: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, South Korea, EU, Japan, UK, Ukraine

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods were exempted from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Country of melt and pour reported for all steel imports
changes.detail: Under Proclamation 10783, importers must report the country where the steel was melted and poured on every entry of Section 232 steel articles, from all countries, whether or not duty applies. From March 12, 2025 the field is mandatory for steel and steel derivatives in ACE.

changes.title: China Section 301: steel and aluminum products to 25%
changes.detail: After its four-year review, USTR moved Chinese steel and aluminum products to U.S. note 31 (9903.91.01) at 25%, covering 213 Chapter 72 subheadings, from September 27, 2024.

changes.title: Mexico: 25% on steel not melted and poured in North America
changes.detail: Proclamation 10783 charged 25% on Mexican steel melted and poured outside Mexico, Canada or the United States, while Mexican steel melted in North America stayed exempt. Superseded on March 12, 2025, when all Mexican steel became dutiable.

changes.title: UK steel tariff-rate quota
changes.detail: Proclamation 10406 let UK steel enter free of Section 232 duty within an annual quota, with 25% above it, from June 1, 2022. Ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: Japan steel tariff-rate quota
changes.detail: Proclamation 10356 set a duty-free quota for Japanese steel from April 1, 2022. Ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: EU steel tariff-rate quota
changes.detail: Proclamation 10328 set a duty-free quota for EU steel melted and poured in the EU from January 1, 2022. Ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: Canada and Mexico exempted from Section 232 steel
changes.detail: Proclamation 9894 removed the Section 232 steel duty on Canada and Mexico from May 20, 2019. The exemption lasted until March 12, 2025.

changes.title: Section 232 extended to the EU, Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: Proclamation 9759 ended the temporary exemptions of the EU, Canada and Mexico on June 1, 2018 and set quotas for Argentina, Australia and Brazil.

changes.title: Section 232 steel tariff begins at 25%
changes.detail: Proclamation 9705 imposed a 25% duty on steel mill articles from March 23, 2018, with temporary exemptions for some countries.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 72 iron and steel were **$27.12B in 2025**, -17.8% from $32.99B in 2024 (peak: $44.93B in 2022). The five largest suppliers were Canada ($5.44B), Brazil ($4.15B), Mexico ($2.40B), South Korea ($1.55B), Germany ($1.52B). By product group the largest were coated flat steel (7210, $4.47B), ferroalloys (7202, $2.57B), pig iron & spiegeleisen (7201, $2.34B). Steel mill products (7206–7229) were $19.24B; pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders (7201–7205) $7.88B.

2025 was also the year Section 232 changed most: every country exemption and quota ended on March 12 and the rate doubled to 50% on June 4, so suppliers that had shipped duty-free under exemptions or quotas, such as Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Korea, Japan and the EU, paid the full duty. The largest single line was nonalloy pig iron (7201.10, $2.34B): pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI and scrap are outside Section 232 and pay little or no duty for most suppliers, while semifinished slabs and billets (7207, 7224) are a large share of the steel that does pay it.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. For steel mill products (7206–7229) the answer is almost the same everywhere: **50%**, because Section 232 has no country exemptions and is collected on top of FTA and USMCA rates. China pays **75%** (Section 301 adds 25%), Russia up to **120%** (70% in place of column 2 plus 50%), and the UK **25%** when the steel was melted and poured in the UK (the cells show the 50% default).

The raw-material groups differ: pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders (7201–7205) are outside Section 232, so they pay their base rate plus, for some lines, the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%), the Brazil duty or China's Section 301 duty. The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties, which apply company by company to many flat-rolled, rebar, wire rod, stainless and ferroalloy imports (see Tariff updates).

Many Chinese steel products also carry AD/CVD, not shown.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 72: Iron and Steel — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Steel: SIMA License, Melt-and-Pour, Section 232 Entry Rules & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 72) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 72 iron and steel line: Commerce SIMA steel import license, country of melt and pour, mill test certificates, Section 232 entry (9903.82.02), FTZ status, marking, AD/CVD scope, plus the legal ways to pay less: UK-melted steel, the Canada/Mexico 25% route, correct classification and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For steel, the paperwork is part of the duty. Every entry of a Chapter 72 steel mill product needs a **Commerce steel import license (SIMA)** and must report the **country where the steel was melted and poured**, and the invoice must carry the **mill test certificate**. The Section 232 heading (9903.82.02, or 9903.82.04 for UK-melted steel) is reported next to the Chapter 72 line, and the duty is charged on the full value with no FTA reduction.

The legal ways to pay less are narrow: the Section 232 product exclusion process and the country quotas are gone, and drawback is not available for Section 232 duty on Chapter 72 steel. What remains: UK-melted steel (25%), Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican quantities (25%), avoiding Chinese origin (25% Section 301), classifying correctly, and checking AD/CVD scope before you buy. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Buy UK steel melted and poured in the UK
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty: 25% (9903.82.04) instead of 50% (9903.82.02) of the full value
levers.appliesTo: Section 232 steel lines (7206–7229) of the United Kingdom
levers.document: Mill test certificates showing the country of melt and pour, and ACE reporting of the melt-and-pour country; at least 95% of the steel must be UK-melted (Tata Steel UK steel melted in the Netherlands counts until January 1, 2028).
levers.caveat: Origin must be the UK and the 95% test must be met; otherwise 50%. The tariff-rate quota for UK steel contemplated by Executive Order 14309 has not been set up.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(d), heading 9903.82.04
Commerce notice on Tata Steel UK (91 FR 23056)

levers.title: Canada or Mexico: the Commerce-authorized 25% rate
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty (25% instead of 50%) on authorized quantities
levers.appliesTo: Section 232 steel articles of Canada or Mexico (note 16(c)(iii)) that qualify for USMCA and were melted and poured in Canada or Mexico
levers.document: Commerce authorization for the producer (submission under the April 23, 2026 procedures), USMCA certification of origin, and entry under heading 9903.82.18.
levers.caveat: Only for producers that supply U.S. automobile or heavy-vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. primary steel capacity; limited to the quantity Commerce sets. Everything else from Canada or Mexico pays 50%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(h), heading 9903.82.18

levers.title: Avoid Chinese origin
levers.saves: 25% of value: Chinese steel pays Section 301 (9903.91.01) on top of Section 232, 75% in total, against 50% from other countries; on pig iron, ferroalloys and scrap 25% to 37.5% more
levers.appliesTo: All 559 lines, for goods of China
levers.document: Mill certificates and production records showing where the product was made. For the tariff, origin follows the last substantial transformation; for steel flat products, cold-rolling hot-rolled steel makes the cold-rolled product a good of the country where it was cold-rolled under the 19 CFR 102.20 rules. Ask CBP for a binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Third-country processing does not change the Section 232 rate (50% everywhere) and can fall under AD/CVD circumvention findings: Commerce opened circumvention inquiries on corrosion-resistant steel from China, Korea and Vietnam in 2026.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 31

levers.title: Classify shapes and raw materials correctly
levers.saves: The 50% Section 232 duty on lines that are not on the note 16(c) lists: cold-formed shapes (7216.61, 7216.69, 7216.91.00.90), pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders
levers.document: Technical specifications (how the shape was formed: hot-rolled vs cold-formed; chemistry for ferroalloys vs alloy steel under chapter note 1) and, if unsure, a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Classification follows the product, not the duty: misclassifying a hot-rolled shape as cold-formed is a penalty case. Cold-formed shapes still pay the 2026 Section 301 duty for most countries.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(c)(iii)

levers.title: Claim USMCA for the non-steel lines
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian and Mexican spiegeleisen, ferrosilicon, ferromolybdenum, ferrovanadium, other ferroalloys, powders and cold-formed shapes (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94)
levers.appliesTo: The 19 Chapter 72 lines that pay the 2026 Section 301 duty, for originating goods of Canada or Mexico
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer (no set format), available to CBP on request.
levers.caveat: A USMCA claim does not reduce Section 232 on steel (note 16(b)) or the Section 338 duty on Canadian DRI. USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52

levers.title: Check AD/CVD scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping or countervailing duty, when the product or producer is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: Flat-rolled (hot-rolled, cold-rolled, corrosion-resistant, plate, electrical steel, tinplate), rebar, wire rod, stainless sheet and bar, ferrosilicon and ferrovanadium
levers.document: The order's written scope (it, not the HTS number, decides) and the producer's company-specific cash-deposit rate; when unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.
levers.caveat: A product in scope pays the cash deposit even if entered under another HTS line. AD/CVD rates change with each administrative review.

levers.title: Drawback: only for the non-Section 232 duties
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the base rate, Section 301 and other ordinary duties on goods that are exported or used in exported products
levers.appliesTo: All lines, but not the Section 232 duty on Chapter 72 steel
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import and export records (19 CFR part 191).
levers.caveat: Proclamation 11021 allows manufacturing drawback of Section 232 duty only for certain derivative articles (Annex I-B, III) of trade-agreement partners; Chapter 72 steel articles (Annex I-A) get none. AD/CVD are never refundable (19 CFR 191.3(b)(3)).

Report the ISO code of the country where the steel was melted and poured on every Section 232 steel entry (mandatory since March 12, 2025)
Invoice must state the percentages by weight of carbon and metallic elements, as a mill analysis or mill test certificate
Section 232: report 9903.82.02 (or 9903.82.04 UK, 9903.82.14 Russia, 9903.82.18 authorized Canada/Mexico) with the Chapter 72 line; duty on the full value, on top of any FTA rate

Country of origin marking on the article or its container; hoop steel, steel bands and wire (except barbed) are on the J-list, but their outermost container must be marked
Russian goods: column 2 rates, 70% in lieu of column 2 on note 30(d) metals, plus Section 232 (9903.82.14)

Rebar and wire rod AD/CVD orders: rebar (Mexico, Türkiye; Algeria, Bulgaria, Egypt, Vietnam in 2026), wire rod (China; Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Moldova, Trinidad and Tobago; Algeria CVD 2026). Not in the tariff calculator

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on iron and steel imports, by country, by product and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Steel mill products (HTS 7206–7229) are Free under the general rate but pay the Section 232 duty of 50% of their full customs value, from every country and on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. UK steel at least 95% melted and poured in the UK pays 25%.

Chinese steel pays 75% (50% Section 232 + 25% Section 301). Pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and powders are outside Section 232; some pay the 2026 Section 301 duties (10%–12.5%), the Brazil duty or China's Section 301 duty.

In 2025 the U.S. imported $27.12B of Chapter 72 products, Canada ($5.44B) and Brazil ($4.15B) first.

faqs.question: What is the current U.S. tariff on steel?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on steel right now
is there a tariff on steel
faqs.answer: 50% of the full customs value for steel mill products (HTS 7206–7229) from every country, under Section 232 heading 9903.82.02, on top of the base rate (Free for steel). UK steel at least 95% melted and poured in the UK pays 25% (9903.82.04). Chinese steel pays another 25% under Section 301 (75% in total), Russian steel up to 120%. Pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap and iron powders are not covered by Section 232.

faqs.question: Is the 50% steel tariff still in effect, and when did it start?
searchedAs: is the 50 steel tariff still in effect
are steel tariffs still in effect
are there still tariffs on steel
are trump steel tariffs still in place
faqs.answer: Yes. Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 steel duty from 25% to 50% for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4, 2025. Proclamation 11021 kept 50% when it moved the duty to heading 9903.82.02 on the full customs value from April 6, 2026, and it is in the current tariff schedule (2026 Revision 21). The Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 ruling in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump ended only the IEEPA tariffs; the steel tariff rests on Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and was not affected.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel from Canada?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on steel from canada to us
is there a tariff on steel from canada
steel imports from canada to us
faqs.answer: 50% on Canadian steel mill products, with or without a USMCA claim: Canada's Section 232 exemption ended March 12, 2025, and note 16(b) collects the duty on top of the USMCA rate. Commerce can authorize limited quantities at 25% (9903.82.18) for Canadian producers that supply U.S. vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. steel capacity. Canadian scrap, pig iron and most ferroalloys stay Free; Canadian DRI pays 50% under Section 338. Canadian corrosion-resistant steel is also under AD/CVD orders since December 2025. Canada shipped $5.44B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel from Mexico?
searchedAs: steel tariffs from mexico to us
what is the tariff on steel from mexico
is there a tariff on steel from mexico
faqs.answer: 50% on Mexican steel mill products (Section 232, 9903.82.02), even with a USMCA certification. Mexico's exemption, and the 2024 melt-and-pour rule that charged 25% on Mexican steel melted outside North America, ended March 12, 2025. A 25% rate is possible only for Commerce-authorized quantities (9903.82.18). Mexican rebar, wire rod and corrosion-resistant steel also carry AD/CVD orders. Mexico shipped $2.40B in 2025.

faqs.question: Does USMCA exempt steel from the Section 232 tariff?
faqs.answer: No. U.S. note 16(b) to Chapter 99 says the Section 232 duty is collected in addition to any FTA or USMCA special rate, so USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican steel pays 50%. A USMCA claim still removes the 10% Section 301 duty on the 19 non-steel lines that carry it (spiegeleisen, some ferroalloys, powders, cold-formed shapes).

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on UK steel?
faqs.answer: 25% (heading 9903.82.04) when at least 95% of the steel was melted and poured in the United Kingdom; otherwise 50%. Tata Steel UK steel melted and poured in the Netherlands counts as UK until January 1, 2028. The UK kept 25% when other countries went to 50% on June 4, 2025; the quota at normal tariff rates contemplated by Executive Order 14309 has not been set up.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel from China?
searchedAs: tariff on steel from china to usa
current tariff on steel from china
what is the tariff on steel from china
what is the tariff on stainless steel from china
faqs.answer: 75% on almost all Chinese steel mill products: 50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301 (U.S. note 31, heading 9903.91.01, since September 27, 2024); 20 wire, strip and bar lines pay 7.5% under List 4A instead (57.5% in total), and forged bars (7214.10) 50%. Chinese pig iron, ferroalloys and scrap mostly pay 25% under List 3, plus 12.5% on some lines. Many Chinese steel products also carry antidumping and countervailing duties (cold-rolled, corrosion-resistant, plate, wire rod, stainless sheet and strip; tin mill investigation in 2026).

faqs.question: What are the steel tariffs on the EU, Japan and South Korea?
faqs.answer: 50% on steel mill products from all three. Their earlier arrangements (EU and Japan tariff-rate quotas, Korea's quota) ended March 12, 2025, and the trade deals of 2025 did not change the Section 232 steel rate; KORUS does not reduce it. Their 2026 Section 301 rates (10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate) apply only to the 18 or 19 non-steel lines.

faqs.question: What are steel tariffs by country?
searchedAs: us steel import tariffs by country
what is the tariff on steel from india
faqs.answer: For steel mill products: 50% for Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Türkiye and every other country; 25% for UK-melted UK steel; 75% for China; up to 120% for Russia (70% in lieu of column 2 plus 50%). Differences between countries show up on pig iron, ferroalloys and scrap, and in company-specific AD/CVD duties.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import steel from?
searchedAs: where does the us import steel from
what countries does the us import steel from
where does the us import most of its steel from
faqs.answer: In 2025 the United States imported $27.12B of Chapter 72 iron and steel. The largest suppliers were Canada ($5.44B), Brazil ($4.15B), Mexico ($2.40B), South Korea ($1.55B), Germany ($1.52B). The biggest product groups were coated flat steel (7210, $4.47B), ferroalloys (7202, $2.57B), pig iron & spiegeleisen (7201, $2.34B). Steel mill products from all of them pay the 50% Section 232 duty today (UK 25% with UK-melted steel, China 75%).

faqs.question: Are there exemptions or exclusions from the steel tariffs?
faqs.answer: Very few. Proclamation 10896 ended all country exemptions and quotas and stopped new product exclusions; general approved exclusions ended March 12, 2025. What remains: the 25% UK rate, Commerce-authorized Canadian and Mexican quantities at 25% (9903.82.18), and goods not on the note 16(c) lists (pig iron, ferroalloys, DRI, scrap, powders, cold-formed shapes). Drawback is not available for the Section 232 duty on Chapter 72 steel.

faqs.question: How are steel tariffs calculated?
searchedAs: how are steel and aluminum tariffs calculated
faqs.answer: Add the base rate of the Chapter 72 line (Free for steel) and the Section 232 rate (50%, UK 25%) applied to the full customs value, plus any other Chapter 99 duty that stacks: Section 301 for China (25%) or the Russia column 2 rate. The 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties do not stack on Section 232 steel. CBP's CSMS # 68253075 says to report 9903.82.02 (or 9903.82.04 / .14 / .18) with the Chapter 72 number, plus the country of melt and pour. AD/CVD cash deposits come on top.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for steel?
searchedAs: hs code for stainless steel sheet
faqs.answer: Steel mill products are in HTS Chapter 72: hot-rolled coil and plate 7208, cold-rolled 7209, galvanized and coated sheet 7210 (7212 if under 600 mm wide), wire rod 7213, rebar and bars 7214–7215, beams and angles 7216, wire 7217; stainless steel 7218–7223 (sheet and plate 7219); other alloy steel 7224–7229 (electrical steel 7225–7226). Pipes, tubes, fittings and structures are in Chapter 73. Use the rate table to search by product name.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on stainless steel?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on stainless steel
tariff on stainless steel from china
faqs.answer: Yes. Stainless steel mill products (7218–7223) are Free at base but pay the 50% Section 232 duty from every country (UK 25% with UK-melted steel; China 75%). Stainless sheet and strip from China, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, plate in coils from Belgium, South Africa and Taiwan, and bar from India also carry AD/CVD orders. Stainless scrap (7204.21) is outside Section 232 and Free for most countries.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on steel scrap, pig iron or ferroalloys?
faqs.answer: They are outside Section 232. Scrap (7204) and pig iron (7201) are Free and, except spiegeleisen, on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so only China (25%) and Russia pay extra. Ferroalloys (7202) pay 1.1% to 10%; ferrosilicon, ferromolybdenum, ferrovanadium and other ferroalloys also pay the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%), Brazil's 25% duty and, for ferrosilicon from Brazil, Kazakhstan and Malaysia, AD/CVD.
